images.seen: start map matches Cliopatria; Roman Republic in Iberia and Italy, Seleucid, Maurya, Xiongnu and Han as expected; no stray cells
Minyue drawn over Fujian and Jiangxi, Han hole in Hunan/Jiangxi before -126 found by counting cells; Cliopatria draws the same Minyue
Han-Xiongnu contest hatch over Inner Mongolia, Tarim in the Xiongnu vassal tint, Hexi corridor Han; consistent with the dossiers (Cliopatria has Xiongnu to Manchuria, compiled does not)
Near East and Central Asia plausible: Parthia holds Media and Babylonia, Indo-Scythian block sits over Margiana (checked, wrong at -144..-128, ruled to Parthia)

before the fix Rome, Italy, Iberia and Greece were drawn in a pale Greek-city-states tint (roman-republic vassal of greek-city-states, 4,510 cells); wrong roles; already closed by data/patches/m0300-m0201.json events (-272), verified in my trial
before: Fujian and east Guangdong drawn as Nanyue (Han vassal tint) in -135..-127 and Guizhou/Guangxi clear; after: Fujian grey until the minyue_-135 keyframe is added, then Minyue's own
before: 1,697 cells (Guizhou, Guangxi, Hunan) drop out of Han for this one year; after: Han holds them; a 24-cell pocket on the Hunan-Guizhou edge stays nobody's to -109
Roman Republic in its own red with Numidia as its tinted vassal; Greece is Roman land in both versions
Kangju, Wusun, Great Yuan inside Yuezhi, Indo-Scythians over Margiana to -110, Tarim in the Xiongnu tint; smaller-state-wins results look right
end map clean: Han contest on the Tarim and Gobi still open (war runs to -89), Roman red, Parthia holds Margiana and Sakastan

issues.what: Han keyframes -127, -126, -121 are built from Cliopatria shapes that lack Hunan and Jiangxi, so at -127 the keyframe snapped away the land the ledger gave Han (Huainan's Jiangxi 196, Changsha's Hunan 157): 830 cells nobody's, then Jiangxi to Minyue in -126. Hunan and Jiangxi added to the three keyframes (and Jiangxi to -111); Han already wins Han/Minyue by R2, so no ruling was needed

han-dynasty_-110 drawn as the Cliopatria shape although its own note says it lacks the Yelang lands taken in 111: 1,697 cells (Guizhou 679, Guangxi 374, Hunan 332) fall out of Han for one year and return in -109. Yelang lands added to the -110 keyframe

nanyue_-170 (wide outline holding Minyue's land as subject kingdom, 'holds to 136 BC' in its note) has no 'to', so it ran beside nanyue_-135 to -127 and gave Fujian and east Guangdong (679 cells) to Nanyue in -135..-127 (Han-vassal tint) and a minyue/nanyue conflict in -126. Cut at -136

after that cut Minyue's ledger event 8 (split, counterpart dongyue, which has no dossier) leaves the whole kingdom, 680 cells, nobody's for -135..-127; new keyframe minyue_-135 repeats the dossier's own -170 shape for those nine years

indo-scythians / parthian-empire: the Indo-Scythian 'found' shape of -144 (Oxus country) took Margiana (291 cells, Mary) from Parthia, who held it from 163-155; the Saka are on the page only from c. 140. Ruled to Parthia for -144..-128

indo-scythians / parthian-empire at -110 (1,134 cells): the Indo-Scythian -110 keyframe held Margiana and Sistan although Mithridates II retook Sakastan between 124 and 115 and struck coins at Marw. Indo-Scythian keyframe loses Margiana and Sistan and gets the 'to' -101 its own note states; Parthian -110 keyframe gets Sistan whole (its -91 outline lacked 133 of the 256 cells); ruling for the Margiana/Sakastan/middle Amu Darya band
Hirat (Aria, 201 cells), Farah (144) and Badghis (69) stay Indo-Scythian in -110 (size rule); the Mithridates I page has Aria taken 163-155 but neither page dates its recovery after the Saka
Indo-Scythian keyframe -126 holds Margiana from -126 to -110 while Parthian pages say Sakastan came back 'between 124 and 115'; the step is bridged at -110, not dated

roman-republic drawn as a vassal of greek-city-states (4,510 cells, pale Greek tint): the -272 vassal_start is recorded by both dossiers and the compiler took the party whose shape holds the region (Rome's) as the vassal. Closed by the -272 event of data/patches/m0300-m0201.json; my own -200 vassal_end was redundant (trial without it identical) and is not in the patch

kingdom-of-sophene ledger/2 skipped: 'Akisene' not in the gazetteer. A patch event with Acilisene alone would change nothing (the 48 cells are Armenia's 24, Sophene's 16, Pontus's 8 and the -188 keyframe, checked after events, excludes them); needs a dossier edit
Persian plateau (Kerman, Fars, Yazd; 4,418 cells) goes from Seleucid to nobody at -164 by the Parthian keyframe and stays so to -145 (Persis from -150, Parthia -144); no page opened on it

Han-Xiongnu contest -124..-119 (5,045 cells) and the second one open from -108 (3,851 cells, Tarim and Gobi), Xiongnu land south of the Gobi nobody's after -119; matches the dossiers and the war's dates; not checked against a new page

size-rule conflicts where the smaller state rightly won: great-yuan/yuezhi, kangju/yuezhi, characene, elymais, kingdom-of-osroene, kingdom-of-gordyene, kuninda-kingdom, nabataeans, thessalian-league, numidia/mauretania (200 cells at -110 fall to 3 once Rome's tint is gone)

scan of all dossiers for keyframes that overlap in years (28 pairs starting in the window): only nanyue_-170 (and indo-scythians_-110, fixed above) let an older, larger shape outlive its role; ten others measured (greco-bactrian -144/-130, numidia, mauretania, pontus, parthia, ptolemy) are harmless because the larger claim loses a conflict or is a subset
a 24-cell pocket on the Hunan-Guizhou edge (about 108.7E 28.6N) stays nobody's from -111 to -109 until the -91 shape of the -108 keyframe takes it

colour_clashes.note: both #d24e3e, 24 shared cell edges; also identical to han-dynasty
#d24e3e both, 12 edges; colonies are drawn in the Han tint, so only their thin outlines tell them apart

problems: hierarchy: no wrong row found in this window.
